summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman was admitted for elective laparoscopic repair of a symptomatic paraesophageal hernia with gastroesophageal reflux disease. She underwent successful laparoscopic hiatal hernia repair with mesh reinforcement. Postoperatively, she experienced transient left-sided chest pain, which was evaluated and ruled out as cardiac in origin. A small left pneumothorax resolved spontaneously, and bilateral pleural effusions were noted, with the right side increasing slightly, managed conservatively. She progressed from NPO to clear liquids on postoperative day one and advanced to a regular diet by day three. Her pain was well controlled, and she was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to follow a modified soft diet, continue home medications including diuretics for heart failure, and monitor for warning signs requiring urgent evaluation. Follow-up was arranged with surgery and primary care.
